query: For refractory high-entropy alloys intended for structural use under extreme-temperature conditions, what single intervention could improve high-temperature oxygen resistance? State one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to the untreated alloy, defines the temperature, atmosphere, and exposure conditions under which it should work, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment with a clear result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The addition of a chromium-rich coating to refractory high-entropy alloys can improve their high-temperature oxygen resistance.
generation.material_initial_state: Refractory high-entropy alloy in its as-cast or as-fabricated state
generation.conditions: High-temperature conditions above 800°C in an oxygen-rich atmosphere
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a protective Cr2O3 layer on the surface of the alloy
generation.mechanism: The chromium-rich coating reacts with oxygen to form a stable and protective Cr2O3 layer, which reduces the oxidation rate of the underlying alloy
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved high-temperature oxygen resistance, as evidenced by reduced oxidation rates and increased lifespan of the alloy
generation.boundary: Temperature range: 800-1200°C, Atmosphere: Oxygen-rich, Exposure time: Up to 100 hours
generation.uncertainty: The effectiveness of the chromium-rich coating may depend on the specific composition of the refractory high-entropy alloy and the exact conditions of the high-temperature exposure

falsification_experiment.design: Compare the oxidation rates of coated and uncoated refractory high-entropy alloys at high temperatures
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the coated alloy exhibits no significant improvement in oxidation resistance compared to the uncoated alloy, the hypothesis is falsified

cited_evidence.text: Gap and lever. Type: failed_attempt. Statement: The study failed to observe the formation of Cr2O3, which is typically considered a protective barrier oxide, suggesting that the specific experimental conditions or timescales prevented its formation.. System: CrMnFeCoNi High-Entropy Alloy. Lever: temperature. Quote: "Although Cr 2 O 3 was not identified as an oxide, a previous work [ [28] ] on phase equilibrium relations in manganese oxide-Cr 2 O 3 at a high temperature reported stability of Mn 2 O 3 up to 877 °C, which agrees reasonably well with the phase transformation temperature of Mn 2 O 3 to Mn 3 O 4 at 900 °C."
